documents.title: Sample Generative AI Syllabus Statements
tiers: Level 2 AI-assisted idea generation and structuring
Level 4 AI task completion, human evaluation
documents.summary: The UMSL Center for Teaching and Learning offers instructors sample generative AI syllabus statements, from UMSL courses and from UMass Amherst, Temple and Washington University. They span a five-level AI Assessment Scale, limited-use and prohibit statements, and advice on penalties and conversations with students. The content of each policy is left to the instructor.
documents.stance_why: The document says "The content of your policy is up to you" and supplies statements from "NO AI" to "FULL AI" plus "Policy that Prohibits AI Use", so it sets no stance itself, hands the decision to instructors and offers tiers, which the codebook codes as delegates.

units.why: The CTL tells instructors to build clear, transparent AI policies for their own courses ("developing clear and transparent policies"), a call for a stated course AI policy, so P09 fits better than P04, which is about who decides.
units.anchor: developing clear and transparent policies on the use of generative AI tools in your course(s)

units.why: "The content of your policy is up to you" leaves the AI decision to each instructor, which is P04.
units.anchor: The content of your policy is up to you
units.policy: The content of each instructor's AI policy is up to the instructor.

units.why: "transparent, curious conversations with your students about AI use ... are highly encouraged": instructors are urged to discuss AI with students, benefits and drawbacks included. P66 fits because it goes beyond listing a rule.
units.anchor: transparent, curious conversations with your students about AI use

units.why: The CTL "highly recommend[s]" department conversations about "appropriate penalties for unauthorized use of an AI". It advises setting penalties but states none, so P37 is the nearest type, with a fit note.
units.anchor: conversations in your department about the appropriate penalties for unauthorized use of an AI
units.fit_note: Recommends departments discuss penalties; no penalty is stated.

units.why: Asking instructors to think about the penalty for "first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate" is guidance on escalation by offense, which P37 lists; no actual penalty is set.
units.anchor: appropriate level of penalty for first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate your policies
units.fit_note: Advises thinking about graduated penalties; none are stated.

units.why: Sample statement: "We will use generative AI tools at various points throughout this course", so AI is built into the course. P79 fits better than P02 because use is planned in, not just allowed.
units.anchor: We will use generative AI tools at various points throughout this course

units.why: "not to replace your own work": AI is part of skill building but must not substitute the student's own thinking, matching P32.
units.anchor: Our goal is to use AI as part of your overall skill building, not to

units.why: "each assignment will include clear instructions about appropriate ways to use AI, explained with the AI Assessment Scale" sets rules per assignment through named levels. P05 is chosen over P04 because the scale is the mechanism.
units.anchor: each assignment will include clear instructions about appropriate ways to use AI

units.why: Students "never replace your own work with AI-generated responses": AI may not produce what is submitted as one's own, P19.
units.anchor: never replace your own work with AI-generated responses

units.why: Students must "follow the AI scale" set for each assignment, i.e. learn and follow the applicable AI rules (P78).
units.anchor: require you to follow the AI scale

units.why: "I will often ask you to describe or reflect on your work process, including your use of AI": a reflection on AI use is required, P26.
units.anchor: describe or reflect on your work process, including your use of AI

units.why: The reflection is a way to show AI "supported, not replaced, your own thinking", i.e. students explain their own work. P34 is the closest type but this is a written reflection, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: show how AI tools have supported, not replaced, your own thinking
units.fit_note: Written reflection rather than interview or oral exam.

units.why: A student whose work is flagged can "meet with you" and then "submit a grade appeal": a right to respond to AI-misuse allegations, P64. The same sentence recurs in each sample and is coded once.
units.anchor: you want to contest that assessment, I am happy to meet with you to discuss

units.why: Level 1 "NO AI": "AI must not be used at any point during the assessment". It is the no-AI tier of a named scale; P05 is chosen as the home, with a fit note that it is also a ban.
units.anchor: AI must not be used at any point during the assessment.
units.fit_note: Level 1 of a named scale; also a plain ban on AI for that assessment (P01/P22).

units.why: Level 2 allows AI "for brainstorming, creating structures, and generating ideas", a brainstorming permission (P15) within a named tier.
units.anchor: AI can be used in the assessment for brainstorming, creating structures, and generating ideas
units.fit_note: Tier 2 of the scale; ideation and structuring only.

units.why: Level 2 adds "No AI content is allowed in the final submission", so AI may not produce submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: No AI content is allowed in the final submission.

units.why: Level 3 permits AI "to make improvements to the clarity or quality of student-created work", an editing permission, P91, with the limit that "no new content can be created using AI".
units.anchor: AI can be used to make improvements to the clarity or quality of student-created work
units.fit_note: Editing only; "no new content can be created using AI".

units.why: Level 3 requires "your original work with no AI content must be provided in an appendix", a submitted pre-AI draft; P26 (keep and submit drafts) is the nearest fit.
units.anchor: your original work with no AI content must be provided in an appendix
units.fit_note: Requires the pre-AI original, not a transcript or reflection.

units.why: Level 4 "requires critical engagement with AI-generated content and evaluating its output", which is a duty to evaluate AI output, P31.
units.anchor: requires critical engagement with AI-generated content and evaluating its output

units.why: Level 4: "AI is used to complete certain elements of the task", so AI-generated content may be submitted for specified parts. P16 fits since conditions (commentary, citation) are attached.
units.anchor: AI is used to complete certain elements of the task, with students providing discussion and
units.fit_note: Content generally, not only code; specified tasks only.

units.why: Level 4: "Any AI generated content must be cited", a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: Any AI generated content must be cited.

units.why: Level 5 "FULL AI": "You may use AI throughout your assessment", with AI as a "co-pilot": open permission and encouragement, P02.
units.anchor: You may use AI throughout your assessment to support your own work

units.why: Level 5 removes any disclosure duty ("do not have to specify which content is AI generated"). P24 is the nearest home, with a fit note that disclosure is NOT required here.
units.anchor: do not have to specify which content is AI generated
units.fit_note: States that disclosure is not required at this tier.

units.why: "Adapted from Perkins et al., 2024" credits where the scale came from, closest to P84 (how the policy was made), with a fit note because no process or body is described.
units.anchor: The AI Assessment Scale (Adapted from Perkins et al., 2024)
units.fit_note: Only credits a source; no body or process is described.

units.why: "Generative AI is permitted/encouraged as specified in assignment instructions, with proper attribution, but other uses are prohibited": AI is allowed only where an assignment says so. P04 is the home because assignments decide; the unit is restrictive by default.
units.anchor: permitted/encouraged as specified in assignment instructions, with proper attribution, but other uses are prohibited
units.fit_note: Assignment-level permission combined with a ban on all other uses (P01/P06).

units.why: "two assignments that encourage you to practice using AI in conversation with your own critical thinking": AI is built into two assignments, P79.
units.anchor: two assignments that encourage you to practice using AI in conversation with your own critical

units.why: "you should not use AI to brainstorm, write, or edit the work you submit" outside the named assignments: AI should not produce submitted work (P19), and the ban is wider than generation.
units.anchor: you should not use AI to brainstorm, write, or edit the work you submit for
units.fit_note: Also bars brainstorming and editing, wider than generation.

units.why: "This includes using AI writing/editing tools such as Grammarly" extends the ban to named prose tools, so P18 (prose rules) fits.
units.anchor: This includes using AI writing/editing tools such as Grammarly.

units.why: "You will regularly do tech-free in-class writing" is an unassisted in-class assessment component, P33; the instructor will also learn the student's voice.
units.anchor: You will regularly do tech-free in-class writing, and I will learn your writing voice.

units.why: "do your own writing ... as part of your contract of honesty with me" asks students to submit their own work, P29.
units.anchor: to do your own writing, regardless of the assignment, as part of your contract of

units.why: Work that violates the AI policy "will automatically receive no credit or feedback", a penalty stated in advance, P37.
units.anchor: it will automatically receive no credit or feedback

units.why: The same sentence treats "false quotations ... or citations of nonexistent sources" as integrity problems, a warning about unverified AI output. P31 is the nearest type, with a fit note because it is framed as a penalty trigger.
units.anchor: false quotations, quotations attributed falsely or without attribution, or citations of nonexistent sources
units.fit_note: Framed as an integrity violation that triggers a penalty, not a duty to verify.

units.why: "We will not use AI tools for any work in this course" is a blanket ban, P01.
units.anchor: We will not use AI tools for any work in this course.

units.why: Reason one: the course "is designed to help you build the skills to think, research, write, and problem-solve independently", skill building through one's own practice, P41.
units.anchor: this course is designed to help you build the skills to think, research, write, and

units.why: "Preliminary research has shown that AI use has led to cognitive debt" cites evidence about AI and learning, P55.
units.anchor: Preliminary research has shown that AI use has led to cognitive debt in academic assignments.

units.why: Reason two lists "environmental costs, racial bias, and privacy concerns" as ethical risks of AI, P53.
units.anchor: AI tools pose many ethical risks, including environmental costs, racial bias, and privacy concerns

units.why: "This includes the use of tools like Grammarly" extends the ban to a named writing tool, P18.
units.anchor: This includes the use of tools like Grammarly.

units.why: The instructor will "talk about this approach in class and discuss strategies ... that do not rely on AI tools": the rule is explained and alternatives offered, P66.
units.anchor: We’ll talk about this approach in class and discuss strategies for brainstorming, outlining, proofreading

units.why: "UMSL does not currently approve any AI-detection software" states an institutional position on detectors. P39 is nearest; it says detectors are not approved, not that they are unreliable.
units.anchor: UMSL does not currently approve any AI-detection software.
units.fit_note: Says detectors are not approved; does not say they are unreliable.

units.why: "I like to operate on a trust system with students and assume the best" presumes good faith, P68.
units.anchor: I like to operate on a trust system with students and assume the best.

units.why: If work looks AI-generated, the instructor "may ask you to have an office hours meeting", so the student is talked to before escalation, P57.
units.anchor: I may ask you to have an office hours meeting with me to discuss the

units.why: "you may receive a failing grade on the assignment" is a stated possible penalty for AI-generated work, P37.
units.anchor: you may receive a failing grade on the assignment

units.why: UMass: "all work produced for a grade will be the sole product of a student's endeavors", own-work responsibility, P29.
units.anchor: all work produced for a grade will be the sole product of a student’s endeavors

units.why: UMass: "Students are encouraged to use artificial intelligence among many other (re)search resources", AI welcomed as a research tool, P02.
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to use artificial intelligence among many other (re)search resources

units.why: "Students must not substitute the substance of their work with the results of such (re)search tools": AI may not produce the submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: Students must not substitute the substance of their work with the results of such (re)search

units.why: Substitution "would contravene the rules academic integrity", classing it as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: that act would contravene the rules academic integrity

units.why: UMass: assignments are "intentionally designed to stimulate and develop critical thinking and individual skills", a skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: Course assignments are intentionally designed to stimulate and develop critical thinking and individual skills

units.why: UMass option "AI is encouraged in specific assignments with attribution": learners "can choose to use AI tools like ChatGPT to help brainstorm and/or draft". P16 fits as conditional use of AI content.
units.anchor: learners can choose to use AI tools like ChatGPT to help brainstorm and/or draft assignments
units.fit_note: Prose drafting and revision, not code; limited to what assignment instructions allow.

units.why: UMass: submissions "will follow the specific assignment instructions regarding the use of AI", students follow each assignment's rules, P78.
units.anchor: submitted assignments will follow the specific assignment instructions regarding the use of AI

units.why: UMass: students "appropriately reference, cite, and attribute any role played, or text generated by AI tools", P24.
units.anchor: appropriately reference, cite, and attribute any role played, or text generated by AI tools

units.why: The Temple template lists activities where AI "is permitted" and others where it "is not permitted", sorting uses into categories; P05 is the nearest fit, with a fit note that these are lists, not named levels.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Dall-e, etc.) is permitted in this course
units.fit_note: Lists of permitted and non-permitted activities rather than named levels.

units.why: Temple permits AI for "Brainstorming and refining your ideas", P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming and refining your ideas;

units.why: Temple permits "Finding information on your topic", AI used as a search aid for understanding, P12.
units.anchor: Finding information on your topic;

units.why: Temple permits "Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts", an outlining and writing-support use, P91.
units.anchor: Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts; and

units.why: Temple permits "Checking grammar and style", a proofreading use, P91.
units.anchor: Checking grammar and style.

units.why: Temple bars "Impersonating you in classroom contexts", such as AI-composed discussion posts or Zoom chat content: students write their own course communication, P58.
units.anchor: Impersonating you in classroom contexts, such as by using the tool to compose discussion board

units.why: Temple bars AI for "Completing group work that your group has assigned to you, unless it is mutually agreed". No type covers a group-work rule, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Completing group work that your group has assigned to you, unless it is mutually agreed
units.uncovered_note: Students may not use AI to do their assigned part of group work unless the group agrees.

units.why: Temple bars "Writing a draft of a writing assignment", AI producing submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: Writing a draft of a writing assignment.

units.why: Temple also bars "Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments", P19. It is a separate listed item.
units.anchor: Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments.

units.why: "You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query": students own what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query

units.why: The parenthetical names intellectual property violations, misinformation and unethical content as risks in AI output. P52 fits for IP; the fit note records the extra concerns.
units.anchor: that it does not violate intellectual property laws, or contain misinformation or unethical content
units.fit_note: Also covers misinformation and unethical content (P31, P53).

units.why: "Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited in order to stay within university policies on academic honesty", P24.
units.anchor: Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited

units.why: "[insert the penalty here*]" in the template: instructors are to state a penalty for unauthorized AI use, P37, with a fit note that none is stated.
units.anchor: Any assignment that is found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways
units.fit_note: A placeholder; no penalty is specified.

units.why: "When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification": students ask before using AI, P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification.

units.why: UMass "encouraged/required" statement: AI "is encouraged/required in this course for specific assignments", so AI is built into some work, P79.
units.anchor: is encouraged/required in this course for specific assignments

units.why: UMass: learners "must appropriately cite any AI-generated material that informed their work", P24.
units.anchor: learners must appropriately cite any AI-generated material that informed their work

units.why: "Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution violates institutional academic integrity policies": failure to disclose is the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution violates institutional academic integrity policies

units.why: Temple broad-use template: "You are welcome/expected to use generative AI tools", open permission or requirement, P02.
units.anchor: You are welcome/expected to use generative AI tools

units.why: Permission is justified because it "aligns with the course learning goal", tying AI use to learning objectives, P83.
units.anchor: doing so aligns with the course learning goal

units.why: UMass prohibit template: "all work is expected to be generated by the learners themselves", own-work rule, P29.
units.anchor: all work is expected to be generated by the learners themselves

units.why: UMass: learners "should not have another person, or entity do any drafting or writing" including "using artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT", P19.
units.anchor: using artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT

units.why: Temple prohibit template: tools "are not permitted in this class", a full ban, P01.
units.anchor: are not permitted in this class

units.why: Such use "may be considered a violation of UMSL's Academic Honesty policy and Student Conduct Code", classing it as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: may be considered a violation of UMSL’s Academic Honesty policy and Student Conduct Code

units.why: "The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in [insert the penalty here*]" is a template slot for a stated penalty, P37, with a fit note.
units.anchor: The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in
units.fit_note: A placeholder; no penalty is specified.

units.why: WashU-adapted text: "Using an AI-content generator ... to complete coursework without proper attribution or authorization is a form of academic dishonesty", P36.
units.anchor: Using an AI-content generator (such as ChatGPT) to complete coursework without proper attribution or authorization

units.why: "If you are unsure ... please contact your instructor to discuss the issue": ask the instructor when unsure, P10.
units.anchor: please contact your instructor to discuss the issue

units.why: "Faculty, students and administrative staff all share the responsibility of ensuring the honesty and fairness of the intellectual environment": a fairness and integrity-culture rationale, P95.
units.anchor: share the responsibility of ensuring the honesty and fairness of the intellectual environment at UMSL

units.why: The opening says learning depends on "mutual trust" and the "integrity of work that is submitted for academic credit", an integrity-culture rationale, P95.
units.anchor: trust the integrity of work that is submitted for academic credit

units.why: "work that is presented as original must be, in fact, original": submitted work must be the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: work that is presented as original must be, in fact, original

notes: One included document. Sample statements from UMSL courses and from UMass Amherst, Temple and WashU are all coded as units of this CTL document. The repeated grade-appeal sentence is coded once.
